entrypoints.summary: Authenticate.Mount registers the /.pomerium/sign_in handler, and SignIn reads the redirect-URI request value.
The finding documents programmatic access accepting unrestricted pomerium_redirect_uri values and a victim browser flow to an attacker destination.

affected_components.role: Registers sign-in routing and parses the redirect URI, forms audience/session data, and issues the callback redirect.
Test context accepting dst.some.example as a redirect destination in successful cases, including a programmatic request.

causal_paths.kind: request redirect URI to JWT-bearing redirect construction

code_slices.fixed: No fixing code diff is present; the report states a deployed fix was verified and recommends redirect allow-listing.
code_slices.surrounding_context: Mount exposes /.pomerium/sign_in; the supplied test table expects HTTP 302 for a programmatic request whose redirect URI is https://dst.some.example/.
code_slices.vulnerable: SignIn parses QueryRedirectURI, appends redirectURL.Host to jwtAudience, creates a session, encodes it into callback parameters, and redirects to a signed callback URL.

observability.channel: browser redirect and subsequent HTTPS refresh
negative_controls: An unapproved redirect URI should be rejected or otherwise prevented from receiving a programmatic JWT after allow-list remediation.
The report does not provide a post-fix test artifact or execution log.
observability.positive_marker: Redirect to evil.com contains pomerium_jwt; afterward, the target Pomerium site returns information after cookie replacement and refresh.

preconditions: Victim has an existing Pomerium session or completes Okta sign-in during the flow.
Attacker controls the supplied redirect URI's destination origin.
For the strongest downstream application-access result, the relying party fails to validate JWT audience.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A valid attacker-origin HTTPS redirect URI, exemplified by evil.com in the report.
trigger_steps.summary: Provide an attacker-controlled pomerium_redirect_uri through the programmatic sign-in flow and cause the victim to follow the resulting login flow.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Redirect URL containing pomerium_jwt, followed by _pomerium cookie substitution.
trigger_steps.summary: Observe the redirect to the attacker origin and capture the URL-bearing pomerium_jwt; the report then describes replacing a Pomerium cookie with it.

impact.affected_asset: Pomerium-authenticated session/JWT and identity information, plus downstream relying-party access when audience validation is incomplete.
impact.attacker_capability: Obtain an authenticated victim's token at an attacker-controlled redirect destination and use the report's cookie-substitution observable; potentially impersonate the victim to an audience-validation-deficient integration.
impact.security_effect: Open-redirect-mediated disclosure of a programmatic JWT and associated victim identity; conditional unauthorized application access where an integrating relying party validates issuer but not audience.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker supplies a pomerium_redirect_uri targeting an attacker-controlled origin to the programmatic-access sign-in flow.
The flow accepts a syntactically valid redirect URL and adds its host to jwtAudience, rather than restricting programmatic redirect destinations to authorized relying parties.

After obtaining the current session and access token, SignIn creates a route session with that audience, serializes it as a signed JWT, places its encrypted encoding and the supplied redirect URL into callback parameters, and emits an HMAC-signed redirect.

The report observes a logged-in or authenticating victim redirected to evil.com with pomerium_jwt in the URL; the recovered token can be substituted into the Pomerium cookie to obtain returned information. Application-access consequences additionally depend on a relying party not validating JWT audience.

failure.operation: SignIn constructs a signed callback redirect containing an encrypted route-session JWT and the caller-supplied redirect URL after accepting that URL's host as an audience.

primary_invariant.statement: A programmatic authentication session or JWT must only be minted for and delivered through an authorized relying-party redirect destination and audience.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The reported feature did not restrict pomerium_redirect_uri; the inspected SignIn context parses the supplied URL and uses redirectURL.Host as a JWT audience, while handler tests designate an arbitrary destination host as a successful programmatic request.

raw_refs.role: primary finding report and fix verification

quality.review_notes: The primary audit report provides a concrete browser/cookie observable and says Cure53 verified Pomerium's deployed fix. No fixing diff or dedicated post-fix rejection test is bundled. The supplied handler test establishes that the inspected context accepted dst.some.example with HTTP 302; it is an oracle contract, not an observed test run. Do not conflate the distinct POM-01-002 signature-validation regression with this redirect/JWT mechanism. Downstream application impersonation is conditional on absent audience validation.

remediation.invariant_restored: Only permitted relying-party redirect destinations can receive a programmatic authentication artifact, preventing attacker-controlled origins from becoming JWT audiences or delivery endpoints.
mitigation_classes: bind JWT audiences and token delivery to authorized relying parties

oracle.channel: browser-mediated HTTP redirect and authenticated Pomerium request
oracle.expected_negative: After redirect allow-list remediation, an unapproved pomerium_redirect_uri should not produce a redirect or programmatic JWT delivery to the attacker-controlled origin.
oracle.expected_positive: For the vulnerable behavior, a victim following the attacker-obtained login flow reaches evil.com with pomerium_jwt in the URL; replacing the target Pomerium _pomerium cookie with the obtained value and refreshing returns information.
